content: Teaching vs decorative diagrams: informative diagrams add new information not available in the text (data/ink ratio principle). A diagram teaches when: it shows a process or transformation (before/after), it spatially encodes relationships that text cannot (network, flow), it provides a worked mini-example visually. A diagram decorates when: it merely repeats what the text says in a different color, it shows a generic formula layout, it is abstract-logo style with no concrete data reference. Statistical concept diagrams should show concrete data examples, label key features, and use annotation arrows to connect visual elements to conceptual names.
